## Claims
- [source-backed] For \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\), the paper conjectures that both Theorem 5.4 generating sets of \(J_v\) are minimal; each has \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements, where \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\) and \(b=\min(i,j)\). [source-6, lines 14-27; source-6, lines 35-42]
- [source-backed] The stronger proposed reduction is \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\); the authors report that a proof had eluded them. [source-6, lines 56-72]
- [source-backed] \(\Lambda\) has Schur \(\mathbb Z\)-basis, \(I_{r,n-r}\) is the ideal spanned by \(s_\lambda\) with \(\lambda\not\subseteq(n-r)^r\), and \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) has basis \(s_\lambda\) for \(\lambda\subseteq(n-r)^r\). [source-2, lines 1312-1330]
- [source-backed] The supplied paper states that \(J_v\) is generated in \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) by each of the two explicitly bounded Schur lists \(i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\) and \(i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\). [source-2, lines 1390-1400]
- [source-backed] The reported finite verification range is all bigrassmannian permutations with \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\); this is finite evidence, not a universal proof. [source-6, lines 46-54]
- [source-backed] The only nonlocal search candidate with an abstract, “Model Reduction for Switched Differential-Algebraic Equations with Known Switching Signal,” concerns switched differential-algebraic equations and model reduction, not symmetric functions, Schubert ideals, indecomposables, or \(\operatorname{Tor}_0^\Lambda\); it supplies no applicable theorem. [doi:10.52825/dae-p.v3i.688]
- [proved] If an abelian group \(Q\) is spanned by \(N\) elements and \(\dim_{\mathbb Q}(Q\otimes\mathbb Q)=N\), then \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^N\): the surjection \(\mathbb Z^N\to Q\) has kernel \(K\); tensoring gives \(\mathbb Q^N\to Q\otimes\mathbb Q\) an isomorphism, so \(K\otimes\mathbb Q=0\); since \(K\subseteq\mathbb Z^N\) is torsion-free, \(K=0\).
- [conjectural] Establishing \(\dim_{\mathbb Q}(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\otimes\mathbb Q)=\binom{a+b}{a}\) would prove the stronger proposed freeness statement and hence minimality of either displayed \(N\)-element generating set.
- [unsupported] No retrieved exact external theorem statement computes \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\), \(\operatorname{Tor}_0^\Lambda(\mathbb Z,J_v)\), or the relevant graded Betti numbers.

## Strategy
1. Set \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\), \(M=J_v\subseteq A\), and, using the quotient action of \(\Lambda\) on \(A\), define
   \[
   Q=M/\Lambda_+M,\qquad
   Q_d=M_d\Big/\sum_{k=1}^{d}\operatorname{im}\!\left(\Lambda_k\otimes M_{d-k}\to M_d\right).
   \]
   The sum is finite degreewise. Use the Schur bases indexed by partitions inside \((n-r)^r\).

2. Audit the missing formal hypotheses before any universal assertion: obtain exact source locators for the definition of \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), conditions on \(r,s,t,n,i,j\), the grading convention, and homogeneity of \(M\). The supplied excerpts do not contain these definitions.

3. For each degree \(d\), form an integral presentation of \(M_d\): start with the ambient free lattice
   \[
   A_d=\bigoplus_{\substack{\lambda\subseteq(n-r)^r\\|\lambda|=d}}\mathbb Zs_\lambda,
   \]
   express \(M_d\) as the lattice generated by products of each listed generator with \(A_{d-|\mu|}\), and impose the product relations after projection modulo \(I_{r,n-r}\). Then append as quotient relations every product map
   \[
   \Lambda_k\otimes M_{d-k}\longrightarrow M_d,\quad 1\le k\le d.
   \]
   Row-reduction over \(\mathbb Q\) yields \(\dim_{\mathbb Q}Q_d\).

4. The precise algebraic target is
   \[
   \sum_d\dim_{\mathbb Q}Q_d=\binom{a+b}{a}.
   \]
   Since either asserted generating list supplies \(N\) generators of \(Q\), the proved lemma turns this rational-rank equality into \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^N\), without a separate torsion computation.

5. Bounded check: reproduce only the paper’s reported family \(r\le4,\ n-r\le5\), after the parameter audit. Preserve for every instance the degree-indexed matrices, Schur-index ordering, multiplication rule, and rational ranks. Such records would test the presentation implementation only.

6. Literature branch: search specifically for exact theorem text under the terms “indecomposables of Schubert ideals,” “minimal graded generators Schubert ideal,” and “\(\operatorname{Tor}_0\) symmetric functions Schubert.” Record a theorem only with its full hypotheses and locator; otherwise retain the reduction above as conditional and literature status as unresolved.

7. Submit the notation audit, every matrix artifact, and the rank computation to an independent reviewer to verify bases, quotient maps, and parameter filtering before using any bounded result.

## Gaps
- No exact external theorem text or applicable literature reduction was retrieved.
- The formal source locators for admissible parameters, grading, and homogeneity are absent from the supplied excerpts.
- No matrices, sandbox computation artifacts, or Smith/rational-rank outputs are supplied.
- No independent-review record is supplied; therefore this is a bounded proposed attempt, not an independently reviewed completed computation.

## Next
Retrieve the missing formal-source passages, then construct and independently review the degreewise presentations for the finite range \(r\le4,\ n-r\le5\); separately retrieve exact theorem text for any literature-based reduction.
